title: memzero_explicit instead of memset everywhere key material is cleared
description: Every buffer containing key material, IKM, derived key output, IV, or ioctl structs carrying key bytes is cleared with memzero_explicit(), not memset(). This includes the inbuf_clear() helper (with an explicit comment), the outbuf on session close, the ioctl struct on stack (e.g. op in ioctl_init, ioctl_sign, ioctl_kdf), and the sym_key_free path. memzero_explicit() is a compiler barrier defined in linux/string.h that prevents the optimizer from eliding the zeroing when the buffer is not subsequently read. The C standard explicitly permits compilers to remove dead stores; any plain memset() call where the buffer goes out of scope immediately after is a candidate for elision. FIPS 140-3 requires CSPs to be destroyed before memory is released; an elided memset is a compliance failure. A reviewer who says 'memset is cleaner and equivalent' is wrong.
